analysis.title: Nike Inc. (NKE): Nike Investor Day Takeaways
key_insights: Nike introduced its Full Stride Ahead strategy at its Nov 16-17, 2026 Investor Day, with an FY31 framework: ~$5bn of incremental revenue from the FY27 base, 12%-14% adjusted operating margin, $3.00-$3.50 adjusted EPS, and ~$12bn of cumulative capital returns through FY31. FY27 guidance was reiterated.

FY27 and FY28 remain investment years. FY28 revenue is expected to decline at a more moderate rate than FY27, operating margin is expected to contract again, and adjusted EPS to decline modestly. FY29 is the guided inflection, with revenue back to market growth and EPS growing significantly faster than revenue.

Performance Sports is expected to deliver ~$4bn of the ~$5bn of incremental revenue through FY31. The five priority sports are Running, Training, Global Football, Basketball and Outdoor, with Running, Training and Outdoor leading first.

Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse are expected to add only ~$1bn through FY31. Four classic franchises (Air Force 1, Air Jordan 1, Dunk, Chuck Taylor) fall from ~$13bn of revenue at the FY24 peak to ~$6bn expected in FY27. The FY31 plan does not rely on them returning to peak volumes.

The margin bridge runs from ~6% in FY27 to 12%-14% in FY31: ~400 bps from PACE, ~400 bps from marketplace health (less discounting, better full-price realization), ~100 bps from operating leverage, partly offset by up to ~300 bps of product input-cost pressure. Only the PACE component is within the company's control.

PACE is expected to deliver ~$2.5bn of annualized run-rate savings by FY31, about half in gross margin and half in operating overhead, with less than 20% of gross savings reinvested. Implementation costs are ~$1.3bn, including ~$300mn of severance in FY26.

Greater China remains a reset. The framework assumes revenue roughly flat from FY27 to FY31, with stabilization beginning in FY29 and a moderate recovery after. About one-third of Greater China inventory is expected to move to responsive manufacturing by spring FY27, and digital stores consolidate onto Tmall, JD.com and Douyin flagships from January 2027.

Running has posted nine consecutive quarters of growth and six of double-digit growth, adding $1bn of revenue since returning to growth. Management expects more than $1bn of additional Running revenue from FY28 through FY31 and targets the #1 footwear share position above $110.
ACG/Outdoor is described as a ~$60bn market where Nike has <1% share. ACG is expected to add more than $1bn of revenue from FY28 through FY31, with doors expanding from ~3k in FY27 to 8k by FY31.

Capital allocation: ~$2.4bn of dividends in FY27 and ~$12bn of cumulative capital returns through FY31. Leverage is expected to peak above 3x in FY28. Buybacks could become a larger part of returns as earnings and cash flow recover.

Supply chain (FAST) targets: reduce weeks of supply by two weeks by FY31, freeing ~$1bn of working capital, double units created in under 14 months, and raise nearshore volumes to North America by more than 50%.

GS stays Neutral with a $30 12-month price target (13.0x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA), 16.3% below the $35.85 close on Nov 17, 2026. GS says more patience is needed, execution risk is elevated, and investors will want more detail on the gross margin and SG&A path before turning constructive.
GS notes that FY28 initial guidance framing implies EPS declining year over year, below prior FactSet consensus.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral after the Investor Day. It sees elevated execution risk and wants evidence of the gross margin and SG&A path before getting more constructive. The target is 16.3% below the $35.85 close.

sector_views.rationale: Nike's recovery is guided to start in FY29. GS wants more evidence that the initiatives produce sustained revenue growth and better profitability.

earnings_insights: FY27 guidance reiterated: high-single-digit % revenue decline, adjusted EPS $1.15-$1.35, adjusted operating margin ~6% excluding PACE-related restructuring and severance charges.
FY28 initial framing: revenue declines at a more moderate rate than FY27, operating margin contracts again, and adjusted EPS declines modestly. GS says this puts EPS below prior FactSet consensus.
FY31 targets (company framework, not reported results): adjusted EPS $3.00-$3.50 and 12%-14% adjusted operating margin.

GS estimates: EPS $1.27 for FY27 (May-27E), $1.20 for FY28E and $1.35 for FY29E, against $2.10 reported for FY26 (May-26). Quarterly GS EPS estimates are $0.36 for Nov-26E, $0.28 for Feb-27E and $0.14 for May-27E, after $0.48 for Aug-26.
GS FY estimates: revenue $42.3bn FY27E, $40.3bn FY28E and $40.5bn FY29E, against $46.4bn in FY26.
risk_factors: Downside: more intense sportswear competition or weak uptake of new product innovation.
Downside: slower recapture of transitory margin pressures.
Execution risk on the sharp FY29-FY31 inflection, which would put margins at the upper end of historical ranges within a few years of sales inflection.
Leverage expected to peak above 3x in FY28.

tension_points.bull_case: Management guides a 12%-14% FY31 operating margin from ~6% in FY27. About 400 bps comes from PACE cost savings, which management controls, plus ~400 bps from marketplace health and ~100 bps from operating leverage.
tension_points.bear_case: GS says the plan needs product resonance and execution, FY28 EPS is guided to decline below prior consensus, and FY31 margins would sit at the upper end of historical ranges within a few years of sales inflection. Up to ~300 bps of input-cost pressure also offsets the gains.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says investors will want further comfort in execution and detail on the cadence across gross margin and SG&A before turning more constructive. Failure to show that detail or sustained revenue growth keeps the Neutral view.

theme_stances.key_argument: More patience is needed before Nike can drive an inflection to sustainable and profitable growth.
theme_stances.evidence: more patience will be needed before Nike can drive an inflection
